hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated, acidified KMnO4 does to a C=C bond, it cleaves it completely to make C=O bonds.
Notice the product is a single molecule containing both a ketone and a carboxylic acid, so the starting alkene must be cyclic so ring-opening gives one chain.
Count carbons in the product and join the two C=O carbons back together to reform the ring, then check where the two methyl groups sit.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidative cleavage**

Hot, concentrated, acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ breaks the $\text{C=C}$ bond completely. Each alkene carbon becomes a carbonyl carbon.

$$\text{R}_2\text{C=CR}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{ R}_2\text{C=O}$$
$$\text{RCH=CR}_2 \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{R}_2\text{C=O}$$

**Use the single product clue**

If the alkene was open chain, cleavage would give two separate products. Here we get one molecule with two carbonyl groups, so the two $\text{C=O}$ carbons were joined by a $\text{C=C}$ in a ring.

Product is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Count carbons: 6 in the main chain plus 1 methyl branch = 7 carbons total.

**Rebuild the ring**

The left end $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O-}$ came from a $\text{C(CH}_3\text{)=}$ alkene carbon. The right end $\text{-COOH}$ came from a $\text{CH=}$ alkene carbon with one H.

Join those two carbons back with a double bond: $\text{C2 - C3 - C4 - C5 - C6}$ forms a 5-membered ring with a methyl on the double-bond carbon and a methyl on the next carbon along.

**Match to options**

A 5-membered ring with 2 extra methyls is a dimethylcyclopentene. Only the isomer with both methyls on adjacent carbons, one on the $\text{C=C}$ and one next to it, opens to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$.

options.A: This is a dimethylcyclohexene, a 6-membered ring plus 2 methyls = 8 carbons. Cleavage would give an 8-carbon product, not the 7-carbon product shown.
options.B: This is also a dimethylcyclohexene with 8 carbons total. Ring opening would give a longer chain than the product, so carbon count alone rules it out.
options.C: This is a dimethylcyclopentene with the correct 7 carbons, but the methyls are separated. Cleavage would place the second methyl further from the ketone, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)COOH}$, not the observed isomer.
options.D: This is 1,5-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene, with a methyl on the double bond and a methyl on the adjacent saturated carbon. Oxidative ring opening joins to give exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$ as a single product.
